From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE).

You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`; no internet), the repo layout, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `lini desugar FILE` — "print a file lowered to primitives + .lini-* classes" — byte-identical to the original (`executable desugar FILE`). `src/desugar.rs` has the stub `pub fn desugar(src: &str) -> Result<String, Diag>`; main.rs prints its result and handles errors/stdin/missing files (verify those wrappers too: errors print `file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1).

Output shape (see `executable desugar assets/test_samples/desugar.lini`, and the outputs for every asset file): a stylesheet block `{ … }` with the root scene config (`layout: flow; padding: 20; gap: 36; font-size: 15;` defaults merged with the user's root declarations), one `.lini-TYPE { … }` rule per type used (defaults merged with the user's `|type| { }` rules, in a fixed registry order; long rules wrap onto an indented line), user classes/vars/bindings as they appear (check), then the canvas: every node as `|primitive#id| .lini-a.lini-b.style-classes { inline decls; } [ children ]`, labels lowered to text children, group labels to `|block| .lini-caption.lini-block [ "…" ]`, auto-created link endpoints declared as `|block#a| .lini-box.lini-block [ "a" ]` at specific positions, links printed with their label lowered into `{ along: 0.33, 0.67; … } [ "lbl" "x" ]`, define bodies materialised per instance, etc. Families lower in rich ways that desugar shows verbatim: tables → cells/header classes, entity, page → frame/ticks/zones/marks + title-block fields, mindmap → topics with `.lini-hue-*`/`.lini-level-N` classes and generated branch links, holes → centerline chrome children, drawings → `px-per-unit`, schematics → parts/pins/labels, sequence, charts, floorplans… The compile pipeline of this repo does NOT implement most of these yet (other agents are working on them in parallel), so implement the lowering *for desugar purposes* inside your own module(s) (src/desugar.rs, src/desugar/*.rs), using the parser's AST (src/ast.rs, src/parser.rs) and the type registry (src/types.rs — note desugar reveals the full default rule text of each type; extend types.rs entries if you find missing/incorrect defaults, that helps everyone, but keep edits additive). Formatting details matter: indentation, line wrapping of long declaration lists (find the width rule), number formatting, string escaping, ordering of rules and declarations, blank lines.

Test corpus: all files under /workspace/assets (test_doc_examples/*.lini, test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini, test_samples/*.lini) via `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-desugar/executable -a desugar <files>`, plus many synthetic snippets in /tmp/<you>/. Prioritise: core constructs (boxes, groups, captions, badges, rows/columns/grids, text, classes, defines with bodies, links, auto endpoints, user rules) first, then tables/entity, page/title-block, mindmap/tree, then the rest.

Before committing, also run the compile comparison (`cmpw.py /tmp/bin-desugar/executable assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini assets/test_samples/*.lini`, starting count 71/209) to make sure you didn't regress compile if you touched shared files. Commit on your branch and report the desugar pass rate, shared-file edits, and gaps.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces // Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
}
// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {

}

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

import subprocess, os, glob, sys, tempfile
outs = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/desugar/out/*.out'))
same = 0; diff = []
for f in outs:
    data = open(f,'rb').read()
    if not data: continue
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/desugar')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'x.lini')
    open(p,'wb').write(data)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'fmt', '--stdout', 'x.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if r.stdout == data: same += 1
    else: diff.append((f, r.returncode, r.stderr[:200]))
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
print('same', same, 'diff', len(diff))
for x in diff[:40]: print(x)
EOF

    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/desugar')

        # filter out link label shape
        print('==', os.path.basename(f))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: q.py [-b BIN] [-a "args"] [-g REGEX] [-t TEMPLATE] snippet...
# Runs the original (or BIN) on each snippet; TEMPLATE may contain {} replaced by each snippet.
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, re
binp = '/workspace/executable'
args = []
grep = None
tmpl = None
snips = []
i = 1
while i < len(sys.argv):
    a = sys.argv[i]
    if a == '-b': binp = sys.argv[i + 1]; i += 2; continue
    if a == '-a': args = sys.argv[i + 1].split(); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-g': grep = re.compile(sys.argv[i + 1]); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-t': tmpl = sys.argv[i + 1]; i += 2; continue
    snips.append(a); i += 1
for s in snips:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', s) if tmpl else s
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='q_', dir='/tmp/table')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp] + args + ['r_in.lini'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = r.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace') + r.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    print('=====', s if tmpl else '', '[exit %d]' % r.returncode)
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if grep is None or grep.search(line):
            print(line)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])

    if a == '-a': args = sys.argv[i+1].split(); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-m': mine = True; i += 1; continue
    if a == '-t': tail = int(sys.argv[i+1]); i += 2; continue

arguments.content:
import math,sys
def ss(t):
    t=max(0,min(1,t)); return 3*t*t-2*t**3
def dss(t):
    if t<=0 or t>=1: return 0
    return 6*t-6*t*t
def wave(x0,x1,A=1.4,lam=12.0,ramp=6.0,mode=0):
    L=x1-x0
    n=max(1,round(L/3))
    h=L/n
    pts=[]
    for i in range(n+1):
        x=i*h
        e1=ss(x/ramp); e2=ss((L-x)/ramp)
        e=min(e1,e2) if mode==0 else e1*e2
        de=(dss(x/ramp)/ramp if e1<e2 else -dss((L-x)/ramp)/ramp) if mode==0 else 0
        w=2*math.pi/lam
        y=A*e*math.sin(w*x)
        dy=A*(de*math.sin(w*x)+e*w*math.cos(w*x))
        pts.append((x,y,dy))
    out=['M %.4f %.4f'%(x0,0)]
    for i in range(n):
        xa,ya,da=pts[i]; xb,yb,db=pts[i+1]
        ch=math.hypot(xb-xa,yb-ya)/3
        ua=(1,da); la=math.hypot(*ua); ua=(ua[0]/la,ua[1]/la)
        ub=(1,db); lb=math.hypot(*ub); ub=(ub[0]/lb,ub[1]/lb)
        out.append('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f'%(x0+xa+ua[0]*ch,ya+ua[1]*ch,x0+xb-ub[0]*ch,yb-ub[1]*ch,x0+xb,yb))
    return ' '.join(out)
print(wave(float(sys.argv[1]),float(sys.argv[2])))

# usage: m.py [-f] [-a "args"] [-g REGEX] [-b BIN] 'snippet' ...   (or -t TEMPLATE with {} and values)
# Runs the ORIGINAL (or BIN) on each snippet and prints filtered output lines.
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, re
args = sys.argv[1:]
extra = []; grep = r'path|error|warning|<line|polyline|ellipse|<rect|translate|viewBox|<circle|<polygon'
full = False; tmpl = None; binp = '/workspace/executable'
snips = []
i = 0
while i < len(args):
    a = args[i]
    if a == '-a': extra = args[i+1].split(); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-g': grep = args[i+1]; i += 2; continue
    if a == '-f': full = True; i += 1; continue
    if a == '-b': binp = args[i+1]; i += 2; continue
    if a == '-t': tmpl = args[i+1]; i += 2; continue
    snips.append(a); i += 1

    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')

                continue
            print(line)
        elif re.search(grep, line):
            print(line)

cat > /tmp/desugar/rules.py << 'EOF'
import glob, re, collections
rules = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
order_pairs = collections.Counter()
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/desugar/out/*.out')):
    txt = open(f).read()
    if not txt.startswith('{'): continue
    # stylesheet ends at first line == '}'
    lines = txt.split('\n')
    end = lines.index('}')
    sheet = lines[1:end]
    i = 0
    names = []
    while i < len(sheet):
        l = sheet[i]
        m = re.match(r'^  (\.lini-[\w-]+) \{ (.*) \}$', l)
        if m:
            rules[m.group(1)][m.group(2)] += 1; names.append(m.group(1)); i += 1; continue
        m = re.match(r'^  (\.lini-[\w-]+) \{$', l)
        if m:
            body = []
            i += 1
            while sheet[i] != '  }':
                body.append(sheet[i].strip()); i += 1
            rules[m.group(1)][' '.join(body)] += 1; names.append(m.group(1)); i += 1; continue
        i += 1
    for a, b in zip(names, names[1:]):
        order_pairs[(a, b)] += 1
for k in sorted(rules):
    print(k)
    for v, c in rules[k].most_common():
        print('   %3d  %s' % (c, v))
EOF

cat > /tmp/desugar/order.py << 'EOF'
import glob, re, collections
seqs = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/desugar/out/*.out')):
    txt = open(f).read()
    if not txt.startswith('{'): continue
    lines = txt.split('\n')
    end = lines.index('}')
    names = []
    for l in lines[1:end]:
        m = re.match(r'^  (\.[\w-]+|\|[^|]*\||#[\w-]+|\(-\)|[\w-]+ ?=|--[\w-]+:|[\w-]+:)', l)
        if m and not l.startswith('    '):
            names.append(m.group(1))
    seqs.append((f, names))
# all lini names
import itertools
after = collections.defaultdict(set)
allnames = set()
for f, s in seqs:
    ln = [x for x in s if x.startswith('.lini-')]
    allnames.update(ln)
    for i in range(len(ln)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ln)):
            after[ln[i]].add(ln[j])
# topo sort
names = sorted(allnames)
order = []
remaining = set(names)
while remaining:
    cands = [n for n in remaining if not any(n in after[m] for m in remaining if m != n)]
    if not cands:
        print('CYCLE among', sorted(remaining)[:20]); break
    cands.sort()
    order.append(cands)
    remaining -= set(cands)
for c in order: print(c)
EOF

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# scan route class vs dy for given clearance K and gap G
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
op=sys.argv[1]
G=sys.argv[2]
Ks=sys.argv[3].split(',')
dys=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[4].split(',')] if len(sys.argv)>4 else list(range(0,80,2))
for K in Ks:
    res=[]
    for dy in dys:
        o,e=run('{ clearance: %s; gap: %s }\n|box#a| "A"\n|box#b| "B" {translate: 0 %s}\na %s b'%(K,G,dy,op))
        p=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)[0]
        t=p.split()
        na=len([x for x in t if x=='A'])
        res.append('%g:%s%s'%(dy,'SLZU'[na] if na<4 else str(na),t[2] if na<2 else ''))
    print(K,' '.join(res))

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# scan route class vs dy for given clearance K and gap G, tall boxes
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
op=sys.argv[1]
G=sys.argv[2]
Ks=sys.argv[3].split(',')
dys=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[4].split(',')]
H=sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv)>5 else '120'
for K in Ks:
    res=[]
    for dy in dys:
        o,e=run('{ clearance: %s; gap: %s }\n|box#a| "A" {height: %s}\n|box#b| "B" {translate: 0 %s; height: %s}\na %s b'%(K,G,H,dy,H,op))
        p=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)[0]
        t=p.split()
        na=len([x for x in t if x=='A'])
        res.append('%g:%s%s'%(dy,'SLZU'[na] if na<4 else str(na),t[2] if na<2 else ''))
    print(K,' '.join(res))

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# 2D scan: b translated by (tx,ty); classify route by start/end sides and arcs count
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
op=sys.argv[1]
K=sys.argv[2]
txs=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[3].split(',')]
tys=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[4].split(',')]
extra=sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv)>5 else ''
def side(pt,cx,cy,w,h):
    x,y=pt
    if abs(x-(cx+w/2))<0.01: return 'R'
    if abs(x-(cx-w/2))<0.01: return 'L'
    if abs(y-(cy+h/2))<0.01: return 'B'
    if abs(y-(cy-h/2))<0.01: return 'T'
    return '?'
print('ty\\tx '+' '.join('%7g'%t for t in txs))
for ty in tys:
    row=[]
    for tx in txs:
        o,e=run('{ clearance: %s; %s }\n|box#a| "A"\n|box#b| "B" {translate: %g %g}\na %s b'%(K,extra,tx,ty,op))
        tr=dict((m[0],tuple(map(float,m[1].split(',')))) for m in re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]*)"[^>]*transform="translate\(([^)]*)\)',o))
        rs=dict((m[0],(float(m[1]),float(m[2]))) for m in re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]*)"[^>]*>\s*<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"',o))
        ps=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)
        if not ps: row.append('   none'); continue
        t=ps[0].split()
        st=(float(t[1]),float(t[2]))
        nums=[x for x in t if x not in 'MLAC']
        en=(float(t[-2]),float(t[-1]))
        na=t.count('A')
        aw,ah=rs['a']; bw,bh=rs['b']
        s1=side(st,tr['a'][0],tr['a'][1],aw+2,ah+2)
        s2=side(en,tr['b'][0],tr['b'][1],bw+2,bh+2)
        row.append('%5s%d%s'%(s1+s2,na,'' ))
    print('%7g '%ty+' '.join('%7s'%r for r in row))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# exact SVG path bbox (python port for exploration)
import math, re

def tokenize(d):
    return re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]|[-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?', d)

def arc_center(x1, y1, rx, ry, phi, fa, fs, x2, y2):
    rx, ry = abs(rx), abs(ry)
    cp, sp = math.cos(math.radians(phi)), math.sin(math.radians(phi))
    dx, dy = (x1 - x2) / 2, (y1 - y2) / 2
    x1p = cp * dx + sp * dy
    y1p = -sp * dx + cp * dy
    lam = x1p**2 / rx**2 + y1p**2 / ry**2
    if lam > 1:
        rx *= math.sqrt(lam); ry *= math.sqrt(lam)
    num = rx*rx*ry*ry - rx*rx*y1p*y1p - ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    den = rx*rx*y1p*y1p + ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    co = math.sqrt(max(0, num / den)) if den else 0
    if fa == fs: co = -co
    cxp = co * rx * y1p / ry
    cyp = -co * ry * x1p / rx
    cx = cp * cxp - sp * cyp + (x1 + x2) / 2
    cy = sp * cxp + cp * cyp + (y1 + y2) / 2
    def ang(ux, uy, vx, vy):
        d = (ux*vx + uy*vy) / (math.hypot(ux, uy) * math.hypot(vx, vy))
        a = math.acos(max(-1, min(1, d)))
        return -a if ux*vy - uy*vx < 0 else a
    th1 = ang(1, 0, (x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry)
    dth = ang((x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry, (-x1p - cxp) / rx, (-y1p - cyp) / ry)
    if not fs and dth > 0: dth -= 2 * math.pi
    elif fs and dth < 0: dth += 2 * math.pi
    return cx, cy, rx, ry, th1, dth

def segments(d):
    """yield ('L', p0, p1) / ('C', p0, c1, c2, p1) / ('Q', ...) / ('A', p0, params, p1)"""
    t = tokenize(d)
    i = 0; cmd = 'M'
    cx = cy = sx = sy = 0.0
    lc = None; lq = None
    out = []
    def num():
        nonlocal i
        v = float(t[i]); i += 1; return v
    while i < len(t):
        if t[i].isalpha():
            cmd = t[i]; i += 1
            if cmd in 'Zz':
                out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (sx, sy)))
                cx, cy = sx, sy; lc = lq = None
                continue
        if i >= len(t): break
        rel = cmd.islower()
        ox, oy = (cx, cy) if rel else (0, 0)
        U = cmd.upper()
        if U == 'M':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            cx, cy, sx, sy = x, y, x, y
            out.append(('M', (x, y)))
            cmd = 'l' if rel else 'L'; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'L':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, y))); cx, cy = x, y; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'H':
            x = num() + ox
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, cy))); cx = x; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'V':
            y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (cx, y))); cy = y; lc = lq = None
        elif U in 'CS':
            if U == 'C':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lc[0], 2*cy - lc[1]) if lc else (cx, cy)
            x2 = num() + ox; y2 = num() + oy
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('C', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x, y)))
            lc = (x2, y2); lq = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U in 'QT':
            if U == 'Q':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lq[0], 2*cy - lq[1]) if lq else (cx, cy)
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('Q', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x, y)))
            lq = (x1, y1); lc = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U == 'A':

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# exact SVG path bbox (python port for exploration)
import math, re

def tokenize(d):
    return re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]|[-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?', d)

def arc_center(x1, y1, rx, ry, phi, fa, fs, x2, y2):
    rx, ry = abs(rx), abs(ry)
    cp, sp = math.cos(math.radians(phi)), math.sin(math.radians(phi))
    dx, dy = (x1 - x2) / 2, (y1 - y2) / 2
    x1p = cp * dx + sp * dy
    y1p = -sp * dx + cp * dy
    lam = x1p**2 / rx**2 + y1p**2 / ry**2
    if lam > 1:
        rx *= math.sqrt(lam); ry *= math.sqrt(lam)
    num = rx*rx*ry*ry - rx*rx*y1p*y1p - ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    den = rx*rx*y1p*y1p + ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    co = math.sqrt(max(0, num / den)) if den else 0
    if fa == fs: co = -co
    cxp = co * rx * y1p / ry
    cyp = -co * ry * x1p / rx
    cx = cp * cxp - sp * cyp + (x1 + x2) / 2
    cy = sp * cxp + cp * cyp + (y1 + y2) / 2
    def ang(ux, uy, vx, vy):
        d = (ux*vx + uy*vy) / (math.hypot(ux, uy) * math.hypot(vx, vy))
        a = math.acos(max(-1, min(1, d)))
        return -a if ux*vy - uy*vx < 0 else a
    th1 = ang(1, 0, (x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry)
    dth = ang((x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry, (-x1p - cxp) / rx, (-y1p - cyp) / ry)
    if not fs and dth > 0: dth -= 2 * math.pi
    elif fs and dth < 0: dth += 2 * math.pi
    return cx, cy, rx, ry, th1, dth

def segments(d):
    """yield ('L', p0, p1) / ('C', p0, c1, c2, p1) / ('Q', ...) / ('A', p0, params, p1)"""
    t = tokenize(d)
    i = 0; cmd = 'M'
    cx = cy = sx = sy = 0.0
    lc = None; lq = None
    out = []
    def num():
        nonlocal i
        v = float(t[i]); i += 1; return v
    while i < len(t):
        if t[i].isalpha():
            cmd = t[i]; i += 1
            if cmd in 'Zz':
                out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (sx, sy)))
                cx, cy = sx, sy; lc = lq = None
                continue
        if i >= len(t): break
        rel = cmd.islower()
        ox, oy = (cx, cy) if rel else (0, 0)
        U = cmd.upper()
        if U == 'M':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            cx, cy, sx, sy = x, y, x, y
            out.append(('M', (x, y)))
            cmd = 'l' if rel else 'L'; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'L':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, y))); cx, cy = x, y; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'H':
            x = num() + ox
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, cy))); cx = x; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'V':
            y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (cx, y))); cy = y; lc = lq = None
        elif U in 'CS':
            if U == 'C':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lc[0], 2*cy - lc[1]) if lc else (cx, cy)
            x2 = num() + ox; y2 = num() + oy
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('C', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x, y)))
            lc = (x2, y2); lq = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U in 'QT':
            if U == 'Q':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lq[0], 2*cy - lq[1]) if lq else (cx, cy)
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('Q', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x, y)))
            lq = (x1, y1); lc = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U == 'A':
            rx = num(); ry = num(); rot = num(); fa = num(); fs = num()
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('A', (cx, cy), (rx, ry, rot, fa != 0, fs != 0), (x, y)))
            cx, cy = x, y; lc = lq = None
    return out

sizes = sys.argv[1:] or ['a0', 'a1', 'a2', 'a3', 'a4', 'a5', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e']

    print('  ticks', len(ticks), ticks)

# ticks.py v1 v2 ... : for each max value, run a single-bar chart and print the y tick labels
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
binp = '/workspace/executable'
tmpl = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and '{}' in sys.argv[1] else None
vals = sys.argv[2:] if tmpl else sys.argv[1:]
if not tmpl:
    tmpl = '|chart| { categories: "a"; } [ |bars| { data: {}; } ]'
for v in vals:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    labs = re.findall(r'class="lini-text lini-chart-text" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    # y ticks: those with the same x-ish right edge on the left; just print texts
    print(v, '|', ' '.join(t for x, y, t in labs), '|', r.stderr.decode().strip())
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

import math
def arc_center(x1,y1,rx,large,sweep,x2,y2):
    dx=(x1-x2)/2; dy=(y1-y2)/2
    x1p=dx; y1p=dy
    lam=(x1p*x1p+y1p*y1p)/(rx*rx)
    if lam>1: rx*=math.sqrt(lam)
    num=rx*rx*rx*rx - rx*rx*y1p*y1p - rx*rx*x1p*x1p

    if large==sweep: co=-co

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# 3 parallel links; vary label texts; print positions
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
pre=sys.argv[1]
for pair in sys.argv[2:]:
    l1,l2=pair.split('/')
    src=pre+'\na -- b "%s"\na -- b "%s"\n'%(l1,l2)
    o,e=run(src)
    labs=re.findall(r'<text class="lini-link-label[^"]*" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<',o)
    cuts=re.findall(r'<rect class="lini-cut" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"',o)
    seen=[]
    for c in cuts:
        if c not in seen: seen.append(c)
    print(pair, ' '.join('%s@(%s,%s)'%(t,x,y) for x,y,t in labs), '| cuts', ' '.join('[%s+%s,%s+%s]'%c for c in seen))

// built-in types and chrome classes, before the user's defines
pub static BUILTIN_ORDER: &[&str] = &[
    "block", "oval", "hex", "slant", "cyl", "diamond", "poly", "path", "line", "icon", "image", "sketch", "box", "rect",

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# usage: lab4.py 'prelude' 'snippet1' 'snippet2' ... ; each snippet appended to prelude; prints label positions
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
pre=sys.argv[1]
for sn in sys.argv[2:]:
    src=pre+'\n'+sn.replace('|','\n')+'\n'
    o,e=run(src)
    labs=re.findall(r'<text class="lini-link-label[^"]*" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<',o)
    print(sn, ' '.join('%s@(%s,%s)'%(t,x,y) for x,y,t in labs), e.strip()[:200])

import json, collections
d=json.load(open('art.json'))
pat=collections.Counter()
heads=collections.Counter()
tags=collections.Counter()
attrs=collections.Counter()

for n,v in d.items():

for k,c in pat.most_common(): print(c, [h[:40] for h in k])
print(tags); print(attrs)
"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: nd.py [-n LINES] [-L] [-a "args"] files...
# normalized diff (scope hash masked; -L drops link-related lines and the links group)
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib, re
mine = '/tmp/bin-table/executable'
n = 40
args = []
files = []
drop_links = False
i = 1
while i < len(sys.argv):
    a = sys.argv[i]
    if a == '-n': n = int(sys.argv[i + 1]); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-a': args = sys.argv[i + 1].split(); i += 2; continue
    if a == '-L': drop_links = True; i += 1; continue
    files.append(a); i += 1

def norm(text):
    text = re.sub(r'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]{8}', 'lini-scope-X', text)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if drop_links:
        out = []
        skip = False
        for l in lines:
            if l.startswith('  <g class="lini-links">'):
                skip = True
                continue
            if skip:
                if l.startswith('  </g>'):
                    skip = False
                continue
            if l.startswith('  <g class="lini-links"/>'):
                continue
            if re.search(r'\.lini-(link|marker|cut|halo)', l) and 'lini-scope-X .' in l:
                continue
            if l.strip().startswith(':root,'):
                l = re.sub(r'--lini-[a-z-]+: [^;]*;', '', l)
            if l.startswith('<svg'):
                l = re.sub(r'viewBox="[^"]*" width="[^"]*" height="[^"]*"', 'VB', l)
            out.append(l)
        lines = out
    return lines

ok = 0
for f in files:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + args + [b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([mine] + args + [b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    o1 = norm((r1.stderr + r1.stdout).decode('utf-8', 'replace'))
    o2 = norm((r2.stderr + r2.stdout).decode('utf-8', 'replace'))
    same = o1 == o2 and r1.returncode == r2.returncode
    ok += same
    print('=== %s  exit %d/%d  %s' % (f, r1.returncode, r2.returncode, 'SAME' if same else 'DIFF'))
    if not same:
        dl = list(difflib.unified_diff(o1, o2, 'orig', 'ours', lineterm='', n=0))
        for l in dl[2:n]:
            print(l[:300])
print('normalized-same %d / %d' % (ok, len(files)))

import re
txt = open('/tmp/desugar/s22.out').read()
for block in txt.split('====================\n')[1:]:
    lines = block.split('\n')
    src = lines[0]
    body = '\n'.join(lines)
    canvas = body.split('\n}\n\n', 1)[1] if '\n}\n\n' in body else body
    # summarize ticks/zones
    ticks = re.findall(r'chrome: tick (\w+) (\d+)', canvas)
    zones = re.findall(r'chrome: zone (\w+) (\d+); pin: center; \} \[ "(\w+)" \]', canvas)
    marks = re.findall(r'chrome: mark (\w+)', canvas)
    other = [l for l in canvas.split('\n') if 'chrome: tick' not in l and 'chrome: zone' not in l and 'chrome: mark' not in l and 'lini-tick.lini-line {' not in l and l.strip() not in ('}', '')]
    print('SRC:', src)
    print('\n'.join(other[:14]))
    from collections import defaultdict
    t = defaultdict(list)
    for s, n in ticks: t[s].append(n)
    z = defaultdict(list)
    for s, n, lab in zones: z[s].append(lab)
    print('ticks', dict(t), 'marks', marks)
    print('zones', dict(z))
EOF

# Turn captured icon data (art.json) into the repo data file data/icons.txt.
import json, sys

S = 1e15
data = json.load(open('/tmp/icon/disc/art.json'))
out = sys.argv[1]

def ext(s):
    v = S / float(s)
    r = round(v, 6)
    if abs(v - r) < 1e-9:
        v = r
    t = repr(v)
    if t.endswith('.0'):
        t = t[:-2]
    return t

KIND = {
    '<g fill="var(--lini-icon-fill)" stroke="none">': 'b',
    '<g fill="none" stroke="var(--lini-stroke)" stroke-width="16" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">': 'l',
    '<g fill="var(--lini-stroke)" stroke="none">': 'd',
}

lines = ['# Built-in icon artwork (256x256 units). "@name tx ty bw bh" then elements:',
         '# b = duotone body (fill), l = line work (stroke), d = dots (filled with the stroke colour).',
         '# tx/ty: translate that centres the artwork bbox; bw/bh: artwork bbox size.']
for name in sorted(data):
    v = data[name]
    lines.append('@%s %s %s %s %s' % (name, v['tx'], v['ty'], ext(v['sx']), ext(v['sy'])))
    for head, els in v['groups']:
        k = KIND[head]
        for e in els:
            lines.append('%s %s' % (k, e))
open(out, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
print(len(data), 'icons')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: sub.py PATTERN file.lini [args] -> diff the subtrees whose opening <g line matches PATTERN (orig vs ours)
import subprocess, sys, os, re, difflib
pat = re.compile(sys.argv[1])
f = sys.argv[2]
args = sys.argv[3:]
mine = '/tmp/bin-table/executable'
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)

def subtrees(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        l = lines[i]
        if pat.search(l) and l.lstrip().startswith('<g'):
            ind = len(l) - len(l.lstrip())
            block = [l.strip()]
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(lines):
                block.append(lines[j][ind:] if lines[j][:ind].strip() == '' else lines[j])
                if lines[j].startswith(' ' * ind + '</g>') and (len(lines[j]) - len(lines[j].lstrip())) == ind:
                    break
                j += 1
            out.extend(block)
            i = j + 1
            continue
        i += 1
    return out

r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + args + [b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
r2 = subprocess.run([mine] + args + [b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
s1 = subtrees(r1)
s2 = subtrees(r2)
if s1 == s2:
    print('SAME (%d lines)' % len(s1))
else:
    for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(s1, s2, 'orig', 'ours', lineterm='', n=1))[:80]:
        print(l[:250])

    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)

    ps=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)

    print(v, ' || '.join(ps), '  ', ' '.join('%s:%s'%t for t in tr) if '-s' in sys.argv else '', e.strip()[:100])

# usage: scenediff.py file.lini [args] -> diff of the <g class="lini-scene"> section (original vs ours)
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
f = sys.argv[1]
args = sys.argv[2:]
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
def run(exe):
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + args + [b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode(), r.returncode
def scene(o):
    i = o.find('<g class="lini-scene">'); j = o.find('<g class="lini-links')
    return o[i:j].split('\n')
o1 = run('/workspace/executable'); o2 = run('/tmp/bin-icon/executable')
if o1[1] != o2[1] or o1[2] != o2[2]:
    print('STDERR/EXIT differ:', repr(o1[1][:300]), repr(o2[1][:300]), o1[2], o2[2])
s1, s2 = scene(o1[0]), scene(o2[0])
n = int(os.environ.get('DL', '40'))
out = list(difflib.unified_diff(s1, s2, lineterm='', n=1))
print('\n'.join(out[:n]))
print('scene equal' if s1 == s2 else 'scene DIFFERS (%d diff lines)' % len(out))

arguments.command:
python3 -c "
pl=-162.284; pr=168.0
n=3
band=(pr-pl)/n
cands={}
x0=pl+0.5*band; x1=pl+1.5*band
x0b=pl+(pr-pl)*(0.5/n); x1b=pl+(pr-pl)*(1.5/n)
x0c=pl+(pr-pl)*0.5/n; x1c=pl+(pr-pl)*1.5/n
t=1/16
for name,(a,b) in {'a':(x0,x1),'b':(x0b,x1b),'c':(x0c,x1c)}.items():
    cands[name+'_lin']=a+(b-a)*t
    cands[name+'_lerp']=(1-t)*a+t*b
    u=1-t
    c1=a+(b-a)/3; c2=b-(b-a)/3
    cands[name+'_bez']=u**3*a+3*u*u*t*c1+3*u*t*t*c2+t**3*b
    cands[name+'_bez2']=u*u*u*a+3*u*u*t*c1+3*u*t*t*c2+t*t*t*b
    # de casteljau
    p01=a+(c1-a)*t; p12=c1+(c2-c1)*t; p23=c2+(b-c2)*t
    q0=p01+(p12-p01)*t; q1=p12+(p23-p12)*t
    cands[name+'_dc']=q0+(q1-q0)*t
for k,v in cands.items(): print(k, repr(v), '%.4f'%v)
"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: snips.py FILE [args]  — FILE holds snippets separated by lines '----';
# each is compiled by the original and ours (cwd /tmp/icon/img) and compared.
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
args = sys.argv[2:]
snips = [s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
d = '/tmp/icon/img'
ok = 0
for k, s in enumerate(snips):
    p = os.path.join(d, 'snip_%d.lini' % k)
    open(p, 'w').write(s + '\n')
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + args + [os.path.basename(p)], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-icon/executable'] + args + [os.path.basename(p)], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if (r1.stdout, r1.stderr, r1.returncode) == (r2.stdout, r2.stderr, r2.returncode):
        ok += 1
        continue
    print('=== MISMATCH #%d: %s' % (k, s.replace('\n', ' | ')[:200]))
    if r1.stderr != r2.stderr or r1.returncode != r2.returncode:
        print('  exit %d/%d' % (r1.returncode, r2.returncode))
        print('  orig:', r1.stderr.decode().strip()[:300])
        print('  ours:', r2.stderr.decode().strip()[:300])
    if r1.stdout != r2.stdout:
        a = r1.stdout.decode().split('\n'); b = r2.stdout.decode().split('\n')
        diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, lineterm='', n=0))
        for l in diff[2:14]:
            print('  ' + l[:220])
print('OK %d / %d' % (ok, len(snips)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# labprobe.py: run snippets (template with {}) for values; print label position relative to the dot
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
vals = sys.argv[2:]
for v in vals:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    dots = re.findall(r'lini-hit-(\d+) lini-oval"[^>]*transform="translate\(([-0-9.]+),([-0-9.]+)\)', out)
    labs = re.findall(r'chart-label" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', out)
    res = []
    for (k, dx, dy) in dots:
        k = int(k)
        if k < len(labs):
            lx, ly, t = labs[k]
            res.append('%s:(%+.2f,%+.2f)' % (t, float(lx) - float(dx), float(ly) - float(dy)))
    print(v, ' '.join(res), r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100])
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: strip.py files... -> writes copies without link/annotation statements to /tmp/sk/strip/, prints paths
import sys, os, re, shutil
out = '/tmp/sk/strip'
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
pat = re.compile(r'(\(-\)|\(o\)|<-|\*-|>-|\|\||->|-->|<->|~>)')
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')
    keep = []
    skip_block = 0
    for l in lines:
        code = l.split('//')[0]
        if skip_block:
            skip_block += code.count('[') - code.count(']')
            continue
        if pat.search(code) and not code.strip().startswith('|') and '"' not in code.split(pat.search(code).group(0))[0]:
            # a link statement; swallow a trailing [ ... ] block
            depth = code.count('[') - code.count(']')
            if depth > 0:
                skip_block = depth
            continue
        keep.append(l)
    p = os.path.join(out, os.path.basename(f))
    open(p, 'w').write('\n'.join(keep))
    print(p)

steps.message:
`|icon|`, `|sign|` and `|image|` now match the original byte-for-byte in every case I tested; the only mismatches left come from links and other features outside this task. Committed on `worktree-agent-ac8377c749be8d2b5` as `b884ef9` and `aa1edeb`.

**Pass counts**
- Full asset comparison: 76/209 (up from 71), with no regressions. The five new passes are spec_06, spec_08, prop_src, prop_fit and drawing_sheet (the last three are the "no such file" error cases).
- blocks/: 6/37 (up from 4; spec_006 and spec_008 now pass).
- icons.lini, hero.lini, shapes.lini, mindmap.lini, sequence.lini, skill_04 and spec_55 still fail as whole files, but every icon/sign node in them is identical to the original. The rest of each file fails on links, gradients, tables or mindmap/sequence layout.
- I built test files with all 1512 icons in 15 fit/size/stroke combinations: all identical, including layout and viewBox. 8,000 random misspellings gave identical "did you mean" messages. Of roughly 250 hand-written icon/image snippets, the only failures are links, gradients and generic validations.

**Icons captured: 1512.** I seeded the list from Phosphor names and checked them against the original. I then probed every name's one-edit neighbourhood (1.3M probes) and found nothing new. The table is in `data/icons.txt` (549 KB), loaded with `include_str!`. Each entry has the body, line and dot elements, the centring offset and the exact artwork bounding box. I recovered the box sizes to full precision because rounding them broke a few stroke widths.

**Behaviour worth knowing**
- Suggestions: names within 2 edits, closest first, then alphabetical, at most 3.
- A label names the symbol; it only clashes with a `symbol:` written directly on the node, not one from a type rule or class.
- `fit`: auto maps the whole 256 canvas; contain and cover fit the artwork's bounding box; stretch scales x and y separately.
- An icon is always square, sized to fit its children (gap 0 by default); `scale` multiplies its width and height.
- Images are recognised by their content, not their extension. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP embed as base64. SVG files are inlined as a nested `<svg>` with their ids renamed. Web and `data:` URLs pass through unchanged.
- An image with no children needs width and height; that error is raised just before layout, after link errors. There is no `.lini-image` CSS rule.

**Shared-file edits (small, additive)**
- `main.rs`: two modules, a validation pass between building the tree and resolving links, and the image size check before layout.
- `scene.rs`: an icon's label is stored on the node.
- `layout.rs`: icons and images use the new measure, and their outer size excludes the stroke.
- `render.rs`: icons and images draw through the shape hook; the `.lini-image` rule is skipped; user rules on `|image|` are written inline.
- `diag.rs`: added the R024 code for the `--no-fs` error.
- `util.rs`: `xml_escape` now turns `'` into `'`. This changes all text output, not just icons: the original escapes apostrophes in text, titles and links, and we didn't.

**Gaps**
- Error order in two rare cases. A bad icon followed by an unknown class gives the class error first (the original reports the icon). The original also reports colour, comma-list and "property has no meaning on this type" errors earlier than we do. Fixing either needs earlier checking passes in shared code.
- Not implemented here because they belong to other areas: gradient fills, "property has no meaning on this type" errors (e.g. `fit` on `|box|`, `multiple` on `|image|`), `--static` colour inlining, the label→`symbol` rewrite in `desugar`, and `scale` for non-icon nodes (I handle it only for icons and images).
- The shadow filter colour ignores `--theme dark`; that is in shared shadow code, not icon-specific.

The discovery and capture scripts are kept outside the repo in `/tmp/icon/disc/`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmp_snips.py FILE [-v] [-a args]  -> FILE holds snippets separated by lines '---'
# compares original vs /tmp/bin-sketch/executable on each, prints mismatches (diff)
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, difflib
args = sys.argv[1:]
verbose = '-v' in args
extra = []
if '-a' in args:
    k = args.index('-a'); extra = args[k+1].split(); del args[k:k+2]
args = [a for a in args if a != '-v']
src = open(args[0]).read()
snips = [s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n---\n') if s.strip()]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cs_')
ok = 0
for s in snips:
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(s + '\n')
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable'] + extra + ['r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-sketch/executable'] + extra + ['r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    o1 = (r1.stderr.decode() + r1.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r1.returncode).split('\n')
    o2 = (r2.stderr.decode() + r2.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r2.returncode).split('\n')
    if o1 == o2:
        ok += 1
        continue
    print('### MISMATCH:', s.replace('\n', '\\n')[:300])
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(o1, o2, 'orig', 'mine', n=0, lineterm=''))
    lim = 400 if verbose else 14
    for line in diff[2:2+lim]:
        if line.startswith(('-    .lini-scope', '+    .lini-scope', '-      :root', '+      :root', '-      .lini-scope', '+      .lini-scope')) and not verbose:
            continue
        print('   ', line[:300])
print('OK %d / %d' % (ok, len(snips)))

txt = open('/tmp/desugar/sc4.out').read()
for block in txt.split('====================\n')[1:]:
    lines = block.split('\n')
    body = '\n'.join(lines)
    canvas = body.split('\n}\n\n',1)[1] if '\n}\n\n' in body else body
    # drop component u
    out = []
    skip = False
    for l in canvas.split('\n'):
        if l.startswith('|block#u|'):
            skip = True; continue
        if skip:
            if l == ']': skip = False
            continue
        out.append(l)
    print('\n'.join(out))
    print('-----------')
EOF

arguments.command:
python3 -c "
pl=-165.192; pr=178.0; pt=-94.0; pb=82.8
vals=[8,14,20,30,42,58]; n=6
X=[pl+(pr-pl)*((k+0.5)/n) for k in range(n)]
Y=[pb-((v-0)/(60-0))*(pb-pt) for v in vals]
# monotone tangents
h=[X[k+1]-X[k] for k in range(n-1)]
s=[(Y[k+1]-Y[k])/h[k] for k in range(n-1)]
m=[0]*n
m[0]=s[0]; m[-1]=s[-1]
import math
for k in range(1,n-1):
    s0,s1=s[k-1],s[k]
    if s0*s1<=0: m[k]=0
    else:
        h0,h1=h[k-1],h[k]
        p=(s0*h1+s1*h0)/(h0+h1)
        sg=lambda v:(v>0)-(v<0)
        m[k]=(sg(s0)+sg(s1))*min(abs(s0),abs(s1),0.5*abs(p))
k=4; t=7/16; u=1-t
x0,y0,x1,y1=X[k],Y[k],X[k+1],Y[k+1]; hh=x1-x0
c1=y0+m[k]*hh/3; c2=y1-m[k+1]*hh/3
v1=u*u*u*y0+3*u*u*t*c1+3*u*t*t*c2+t*t*t*y1
v2=u**3*y0+3*u**2*t*c1+3*u*t**2*c2+t**3*y1
# hermite
h00=2*t**3-3*t**2+1; h10=t**3-2*t**2+t; h01=-2*t**3+3*t**2; h11=t**3-t**2
v3=h00*y0+h10*hh*m[k]+h01*y1+h11*hh*m[k+1]
# de casteljau
a=y0+(c1-y0)*t; b=c1+(c2-c1)*t; c=c2+(y1-c2)*t
d=a+(b-a)*t; e=b+(c-b)*t; v4=d+(e-d)*t
# lerp form de casteljau
a=(1-t)*y0+t*c1; b=(1-t)*c1+t*c2; c=(1-t)*c2+t*y1; d=(1-t)*a+t*b; e=(1-t)*b+t*c; v5=(1-t)*d+t*e
# horner polynomial
A=-y0+3*c1-3*c2+y1; B=3*y0-6*c1+3*c2; C=-3*y0+3*c1; D=y0
v6=((A*t+B)*t+C)*t+D
for v in [v1,v2,v3,v4,v5,v6]: print(repr(v), '%.4f'%v)
"

from fractions import Fraction as F
pl=F('-165.192'); pr=F(178); pt=F(-94); pb=F('82.8')
vals=[8,14,20,30,42,58]; n=6
X=[pl+(pr-pl)*F(2*k+1,2*n) for k in range(n)]
Y=[pb-F(v,60)*(pb-pt) for v in vals]
h=[X[k+1]-X[k] for k in range(n-1)]
s=[(Y[k+1]-Y[k])/h[k] for k in range(n-1)]
m=[F(0)]*n; m[0]=s[0]; m[-1]=s[-1]
for k in range(1,n-1):
    s0,s1=s[k-1],s[k]
    p=(s0*h[k]+s1*h[k-1])/(h[k-1]+h[k])

import subprocess, sys, os, difflib

    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# dd.py name... : diff original vs ours for /tmp/chart/cases/<name>.lini (compact)
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
ours = os.environ.get('BIN', '/tmp/bin-chart/executable')
n = int(os.environ.get('DL', '40'))
w = int(os.environ.get('W', '220'))
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    f = name if name.endswith('.lini') else '/tmp/chart/cases/%s.lini' % name
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f))
    b = os.path.basename(f)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([ours, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    print('=====', name, 'exit', r1.returncode, r2.returncode)
    if r1.stderr != r2.stderr:
        print('stderr orig:', r1.stderr.decode()[:300])
        print('stderr ours:', r2.stderr.decode()[:300])
    a = r1.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    bb = r2.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    k = 0
    for l in difflib.unified_diff(a, bb, lineterm='', n=0):
        if l.startswith('---') or l.startswith('+++'):
            continue
        print(l[:w])
        k += 1
        if k >= n:
            break

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fmtprobe.py fmt... : print tooltip texts (titles) for a bar chart with various values
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
vals = os.environ.get('VALS', '1234.5678, 0.0123, 0.5, 2.75, -3.125, 1, 0, 99999, 0.333333')
n = len(vals.split(','))
cats = ', '.join('"c%d"' % k for k in range(n))
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    src = '|chart| { categories: %s; format: %s; } [ |line| { data: %s; marker: dot; } ]' % (cats, f, vals)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    titles = re.findall(r'<title>c\d+: ([^<]*)</title>', out)
    ticks = re.findall(r'style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    print(f, '|', ' ; '.join(titles), '| ticks:', ' '.join(ticks[:8]), r.stderr.decode().strip()[:150])
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
