#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE). test_doc_examples test_images test_samples 173 assets cards.lini chart_advanced.lini chart_hero.lini charts.lini desugar.lini drawing_annotations.lini drawing_gdt.lini drawing_section.lini drawing_sheet.lini drawing_turned.lini entity_hero.lini expr.lini floorplan.lini floorplan_parts.lini hello.lini hero.lini icons.lini layout.lini links.lini links_hard.lini links_medium.lini logo.lini mindmap.lini paint.lini palette.lini pcb.lini schematic.lini schematic_blocks.lini schematic_hero.lini schematic_parts.lini sequence.lini shapes.lini sketch.lini styles.lini templates.lini text_tables.lini tree.lini

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

results.content:
# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: core features that cut across all diagram families — byte-identical to the original:
1. Paint: `gradient(--a, --b[, --c…])` (auto angle), `linear-gradient(angle, …)`, `radial-gradient(…)`, gradients on stroke, oklch()/rgb()/hsl() stops — `<linearGradient>`/`<radialGradient>` defs with hashed ids (find the hashed string; util::hash8 = FNV-1a64 folded), `fill="url(#…)"` usage in rules/inline styles, and how vars inside gradients register. Tests: test_doc_examples spec_21 (+blocks/spec_021), test_samples paint.lini, hero.lini, pcb.lini (the root `fill: gradient(...)` canvas). Root canvas `fill:` with gradients too.
2. Generic validation with the original's exact messages/codes/spans and ORDER of checks: unknown property (with "did you mean" + the JSON "suggestion" object: `{"span":{…},"replacement":"color","applicability":"machine-applicable"}` inside the diagnostic — check diag.rs JSON output against `executable --json`), "'X' has no meaning on '|Y|'", scene-config-only properties (`'density' is scene config`…), value-shape errors (`'width' takes a number — a '%' is a colour component`, `expected 1, 2, or 4 values, got 3`, `'font-weight' takes …`, `'fit' must be …`), unknown function/name in expressions (`unknown function 'wave'` — note expressions in `points:` are evaluated lazily: spec_29 errors at the use site 2:10), `'|line|' requires 'points'` (exists in chart.rs validate — keep consistent), layout-membership errors that aren't family-specific. Build a corpus of hundreds of erroneous/odd snippets and compare first-error output (text and `--json`). Family-specific errors (sequence/tree/schematic/drawing/chart membership) belong to other agents working in parallel — don't duplicate those.
3. CLI rendering modes: `--static` (inline every `var()` as its literal light value — or the chosen theme's — and outline all text to glyph paths: `<path id="lini-g{size*100?}{weight}-{gid}" d="…"/>` defs built from the bundled TTF outlines (src/font.rs has glyph outlines; quadratic → `Q` with implied on-curve midpoints, numbers trimmed), `<use href transform="translate(x y) scale(s -s)">`, the `.lini-canvas` background rect, the shorter stylesheet; verify on many asset files), `--embed-font` (base64 `@font-face` for each used family×weight — "Lini Sans"/"Lini Sans Code" — font bytes are in fonts/*.ttf; check order and where they go), `--theme FILE` (a CSS file of `--lini-*` overrides; error text when unreadable is known: see main.rs), `--theme A/B` pairs (theme.rs), `--no-fs`, `--format html` (exists), `-o FILE`, shadows under themes (flood-color should follow the theme — currently hardcoded light).
Hook these into render.rs/main.rs with care (other agents edit render.rs in parallel; keep your changes as contained as possible, e.g. a post-processing or a dedicated module src/static.rs, src/gradient.rs, src/validate.rs).

Before committing, run the full asset comparison in several modes: default, `-a --static`, `-a --embed-font`, `-a "--theme dark"`, `-a "--theme high-contrast"`, `-a "--theme light/dark"`, `-a --json` (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-core/executable -a "…" /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; default start: 171/246) and make sure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. # Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

1	# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors
2	
3	## The task (read carefully)
4	We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
5	`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
6	produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
7	exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.
8	
9	RULES (strict):
10	- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
11	  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
12	- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
13	- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
14	- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.
15	
16	- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
17	  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
18	- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
19	  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.
20	
21	## Docs / samples
22	- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
23	  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
24	  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
25	  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.
26	
27	## Build & compare
28	- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
29	- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
30	  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
31	- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
32	  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
33	  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
34	  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
35	  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
36	- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.
37	
38	## Code map (src/)
39	- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
40	  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
41	  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
42	- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
43	  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
44	- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
45	  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
46	  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
47	  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
48	- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
49	- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
50	- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
51	  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
52	  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
53	- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
54	  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
55	- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
56	  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
57	  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
58	  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
59	- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
60	  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
61	- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
62	- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.
63	
64	## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
65	- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
66	  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
67	  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
68	- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
69	  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
70	- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
71	- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
72	  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).
73	
74	## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
75	- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
76	  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
77	  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
78	  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
79	  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
80	  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
81	  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
82	  `highlight.rs` (done).
83	- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
84	  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
85	  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
86	  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
87	- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
88	  are 246/246 on the corpus.
89	
90	## Links (already in place)
91	- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
92	  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
93	  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
94	  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
95	  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
96	  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
97	  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
98	  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
99	- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.
100	
101	## Working rules
102	- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
103	  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
104	  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
105	- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
106	  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

#!/bin/bash
# for each file: compare original compile vs original compile of desugar output
out=/tmp/sch/t
mkdir -p "$out"
for f in "$@"; do
  b=$(basename "$f" .lini); d=$(dirname "$f")
  (cd "$d"; /workspace/executable desugar "$b.lini" > "$out/${b}_d.lini" 2>/dev/null; /workspace/executable "$b.lini" > "$out/$b.svg" 2>"$out/$b.err")
  (cd "$out"; /workspace/executable "${b}_d.lini" > "${b}_d.svg" 2>"${b}_d.err")
  if cmp -s "$out/$b.svg" "$out/${b}_d.svg"; then echo "$b SAME"; else echo "$b DIFF $(diff "$out/$b.svg" "$out/${b}_d.svg" | wc -l)"; fi
done

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile,glob
MINE='/tmp/bin-link/executable'
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
files=sys.argv[1:] or sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/link/c/*.txt'))

def run(b,src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run([b,'r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
def strip_mask(b):
    return re.sub(rb'lini-label-cut-[0-9a-f]{8}',b'lini-label-cut-X',re.sub(rb'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]{8}',b'lini-scope-X',b))
tot=0; same=0; same_nm=0
for f in files:
    snips=[s for s in open(f).read().split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
    res=[]
    for s in snips:
        a=run(ORIG,s); b=run(MINE,s)
        tot+=1
        if a==b: same+=1; same_nm+=1; res.append('=')
        elif strip_mask(a[0])==strip_mask(b[0]) and a[1:]==b[1:]: same_nm+=1; res.append('m')
        else: res.append('x')
    print('%-28s %s'%(os.path.basename(f),''.join(res)))
print('TOTAL exact %d / %d   (ignoring mask/scope ids: %d)'%(same,tot,same_nm))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Categorise differences for each failing snippet: which kinds of lines differ.
import subprocess,sys,re,tempfile,difflib
fn=sys.argv[1]
snips=[s for s in open(fn).read().split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
def run(b,s):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s)
    r=subprocess.run([b,'r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(),r.stderr.decode()
def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r'lini-label-cut-[0-9a-f]{8}','X',re.sub(r'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]{8}','S',s))
for i,s in enumerate(snips):
    o1,e1=run('/workspace/executable',s); o2,e2=run('/tmp/bin-link/executable',s)
    if (o1,e1)==(o2,e2): continue
    kinds=set()
    if e1!=e2: kinds.add('stderr')
    a=norm(o1).split('\n'); b=norm(o2).split('\n')
    if a==b: kinds.add('ids-only')
    for l in difflib.unified_diff(a,b,lineterm='',n=0):
        if l.startswith(('---','+++','@@')): continue
        if '<path' in l: kinds.add('path')
        elif 'viewBox' in l: kinds.add('viewbox')
        elif 'lini-link-label' in l: kinds.add('label')
        elif 'marker' in l: kinds.add('marker')
        elif 'mask' in l: kinds.add('mask')
        elif 'lini-scope' in l or l.strip().startswith(('.','-','+')) and '{' in l: kinds.add('css')
        else: kinds.add('other')
    print(i,sorted(kinds),s.strip().replace('\n',' | ')[:150])

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}
